name: Resume Builder
tagline: A resume that sells you for one specific job — impact-first bullets, a clean one-page PDF, and a tailored version per application.
who: Anyone who has to hand someone a resume: a student applying to a club or a first internship, a new grad, a mid-career operator changing lanes, a veteran with twenty years to fit on two pages. Also the parent, manager, or friend who keeps getting asked to look at one.
how: Your agent starts by asking what you're applying to and where you are in your career, then reads whatever you drop in — old resumes, a LinkedIn export, reviews, project notes — into a master record of everything true about you, tagged with where each fact came from. A short impact interview turns duties into results with numbers (Google's "accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z" shape), a target brief pulls the posting's own vocabulary and the two or three reasons you're the obvious call, and the bundled renderer turns the draft into a print-quality PDF in one of six looks, matched to the field and to how you want to come across — single column, real text, the way screeners and seven-second skimmers both read best. A live preview tab shows the printed pages as they change while you work together, with a menu to switch the look and a color picker for the accent, and at the end you get the PDF and a Word copy to download, plus a master record that makes the next application a tailored version in minutes. Nothing is ever invented: every number traces to something you said or gave it.
